description: Strong candidate that loses without invalidating the quality of the process.
market_title: Will the April 2026 CPI report print above consensus?
resolution_rule_summary: Resolves YES if the stated CPI print exceeds published consensus.

market_observation.market_note: Price remained cheap versus a coherent bundle of inflation signals.

entry_rationale: Several public inflation indicators implied the market was underpricing a hot print.

decision_horizon.rationale: The setup should remain live until the next major macro surprise.

invalidation_condition: Stand down if intervening data sharply weakens the inflation read-through.
abstention_alternative: Skip entry only if consensus fully reprices before operator review.
evidence_summary: Evidence was coherent, current, and legible.
scoring_notes: This is the canonical disciplined-loss case.
gate_reasons: Evidence and market structure were both strong.
Execution readiness remained operator-mediated and bounded.

review_plan.thesis_quality_assessment: The thesis stayed coherent, evidence-backed, and properly bounded.
review_plan.score_quality_assessment: The score accurately reflected a strong candidate despite the final loss.
review_plan.timing_quality_assessment: Timing was acceptable and did not clearly cause the failure.
review_plan.governance_quality_assessment: All governance boundaries were respected end to end.
review_plan.profit_loss_note: Loss does not erase disciplined reasoning.
review_plan.attention_cost_estimate: Moderate operator attention for a fully reviewed bounded trade.
review_plan.abstention_counterfactual: Abstention would have avoided the loss but not improved the process quality.
review_plan.review_notes: This case protects the stack from learning that every loss equals bad reasoning.
